featured_reviews.name: Omkar Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dan Dan Chinese today on the occasion of Ram Navami, as many nearby Chinese food corners were closed. I decided to give this place a try, and I ordered two dishes: American Choupsey and Chicken Hakka Noodles.

Both dishes were delicious, and I must say, it was my first time trying Choupsey, which I highly recommend to anyone visiting this place. The Chicken Hakka Noodles were also tasty, and they offer good quality and quantity. The portion sizes are quite generous, so one person may struggle to finish a dish — it's best to come with a companion or plan to parcel the leftover food.

As a local guide on Google Maps and someone who likes to share detailed reviews, I'd like to highlight a few points that may be helpful for potential customers, and also for the owner to consider:

1. Lack of Air Conditioning: There is no air conditioning in the restaurant, and in the humid climate of Vile Parle East, it can get uncomfortable, especially near the fan area. Adding an air conditioning system could significantly improve the dining experience.

2. Cold Drinks: The restaurant doesn't offer cold drinks on the menu but provides them by bringing them from an outside source. While I appreciate that they offer this option when many others refuse, it would be more convenient if they stocked cold drinks on-site.

3. Slow Service: The food took quite a long time to be served, and there was no dedicated staff member to assist customers. There was an uncle helping out, but he was juggling multiple tasks — taking orders, answering calls, handling the kitchen, and managing bills. This made the service a bit frustrating at times, and I ended up packing my noodles to go. It would be beneficial to have an extra staff member to assist with customer service.

4. Mosquitoes: The restaurant is open, and with no gates, mosquitoes can be a problem. The plants outside, while adding to the aesthetic, also provide a hiding place for mosquitoes. Addressing this issue, perhaps with a net or better control, would improve the comfort of diners.

5. Order Assistance: Typically, restaurants guide customers on specials, combos, and menu items when taking orders. However, I was not informed about the combos or daily specials until after my order was placed. It would be helpful if the staff proactively shared this information to enhance the dining experience.

6. Customer Service: While the food was good, there were some basic service issues. No one asked if I wanted water, and there were no tissues or sauces available on the table. That said, I’d like to commend the uncle at the counter, who made an effort to clean my plate, spoon, and fork before serving. His politeness and attention to detail were appreciated.

Suggestions for Improvement:

Install air conditioning to improve comfort in the humid climate.

Stock cold drinks on-site to make it more convenient for customers.

Reduce the waiting time and consider adding more staff for customer service.

Address the mosquito issue, perhaps with better pest control or netting.

Ensure that customers are informed about specials and combos when ordering.

Provide basic amenities like water, tissues, and sauces to enhance the overall dining experience.

Overall, Dan Dan Chinese offers tasty food, but there are some areas for improvement, especially regarding service, comfort, and customer care. With a few adjustments, it could provide a much more enjoyable dining experience.

Note: I’ve added photos of the restaurant, the food I ordered, and the menu for reference to help others get a better idea before visiting.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited China Dine at Hanuman Road and ordered the Prawns Triple Schezwan Rice.
The restaurant is simple and mainly suits quick, casual dining.
Service was okay and the staff were reasonably prompt.
Presentation of the dish was also fine, nothing fancy but acceptable.
However, the taste was quite disappointing.
The Schezwan flavor was very pale, lacking the usual spice and punch.
The prawns did not taste fresh and had very mild seasoning.
The gravy was thin and watery instead of rich and flavorful.
The rice and sauce did not blend well together.
Overall, the dish felt bland and lacked depth.
Portion size was alright, but taste did not match the price.
If someone prefers strong, spicy Schezwan-style food, this will fall short.
The dish definitely needs better seasoning and fresher prawns.
There are better places nearby for Indo-Chinese with stronger flavor.
Overall: 2/5 for taste, though service and presentation were okay.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Flavours of China in Dadar West for a friend’s birthday celebration, and it turned out to be a delightful dining experience. Though the place is modest in size, the ambience has a distinct charm with classic Chinese-style décor and wall hangings that add to the vibe.

We started off with Chicken Lollipop with Gravy and Chicken Crispy – both starters were well-prepared, flavorful, and had the perfect balance of spice and texture.

For the main course, we opted for Malaysian Fried Rice, Red Thai Curry with Jasmine Rice, and Asian Pot Rice. The Malaysian Fried Rice had green-color, offering a unique twist, while the Red Thai Curry was undoubtedly the highlight – rich, aromatic, and beautifully presented.

Special mention to Mr. Shrikant for his prompt and attentive service, which added to the overall positive experience.

If you're looking for a cozy Chinese dining spot in Dadar with good food and courteous service, Flavours of China is worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Pratik Gadgil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visit 1

I visited the place today. Mocktails & appetizers were amazing. The vegetable dumplings were unique. Mr Yogesh, the manager, offered me personalised services; the other servers were equally helpful and absolutely friendly. The main Course was average - I tasted some French Beans and Chicken. In the deserts, the Wasabi Cheese Case was fantastic.

Visit 3 [ Extract ]

Some of the dishes I had:

Duck [ in the main course, whose precise name I don't remember ] - Unusually strong on species, very much unauthentic, some pieces covered almost entirely in bones, and tough to chew upon. Call it a botched preparation and mood spoiler! It's not very often that I leave behind any dish. The grievance was resolved amicably.

Pork baos - You don't get these in many same-level restaurants, so a must-try. On a sweeter side and minced well and soft to consume. Arrived in the estimated time.

The quantity for all the dishes was above average and probably the largest I have seen at same-level restaurants.

Visit 4

A supreme and unforgettable experience

Some of the dishes I tried:

Traditional Pecking Duck - A conventional Chinese dish which is usually served with pancakes, troika of sauces, some veggies, and ofcourse, the duck cuts. Kudos to the chef, on my request, for serving me ready-made and saving me all the effort. The dish was slightly on the sweeter side, and the rolls had a good proportion of duck. Much laborious to scoff if all constituents are served separately.

Steamed Chilean Sea Bass - Prepared in soya ginger sauce, lightly spicy, mildly  pungent, and medium in size. Delicious, healthy and a must try. Maybe a few veggies at the side should be considered.

Light Breeze mocktail - Indeed light, mild soda, simple as it gets. Kinda like virgin mojito less Sprite/7UP and less coriander.

Grapefruit-based mocktail - the best of the three, authentic grapefruit flavour with medium bitterness, preserving the original taste, no soda.

Watermelon-based mocktail - another light one with no soda, pure watermelon [ and no syrup ] and a dash of cucumber.

I would like to thank Mr Jojo for preparing tailor-made off-the-menu [ above-mentioned ] mocktails, all of which were served inside 10 mins. And not to forget, offering me cashews which were off-the-menu. At the end, he also made an exception and served me the desserts from another restaurant because I didn't want any from the menu courtesy to various reasons.

This is amongst the handful of restaurants in this range where almost all the dishes are available in small and large sizes, and this allows one to make better selections on quantity. To add to that, even small sizes are equivalent to medium in many dishes. If I were to offer a suggestion, it would be to rejig the currently-mediocre dessert menu and add dishes like creme brulee, coconut pudding and cheese cake. On the embellishments front, I would say the restaurant is slightly behind despite the fact that they have a Chinese dragon hanging from the top & and a plush red carpet albeit the latter doesn't cover the flooring of the whole restaurant . The pots don't look very attractive and there is room for vibrance - a few paintings & art pieces could help. The restaurant size is quite big with 10+ tables.

It was also nice to meet & have an interlocution with Mr Srinivas, and I would like to thank him for personally overseeing the dinner and ensuring that it was a memorable experience. It is recherche of someone of his level to come down and discuss the ways certain past flaws were handled and briefing on the feedback taken to minimise the bitter moments; I really appreciate this commitment.

I am looking forward to visiting here again soon.

Overall, Flavours Of China near Pestom Sagar Road No. 4 is a solid choice for Chinese food lovers. With delicious soup, tasty dishes, friendly service, and a pleasant ambience, it’s definitely worth visiting if you’re in Chembur.

featured_reviews.name: Ambalal
featured_reviews.review_text:
# A Hidden Gem: Rare Kitchen

**Rating: 4.5/5 stars**

Tucked away on a quiet side street downtown, Rare Kitchen proved to be one of those delightful discoveries that makes you feel like you've uncovered a local secret. From the moment we stepped through the rustic wooden door, the warm ambiance and aromatic blend of garlic, herbs, and fresh bread set the stage for what would become a memorable evening.

## The Atmosphere
The interior strikes a perfect balance between cozy and elegant, with exposed brick walls adorned with vintage Italian photographs and soft lighting from wrought-iron fixtures. The gentle hum of conversation creates an intimate setting that's ideal for both romantic dinners and casual gatherings with friends.

## The Food
Our server, Maria, was knowledgeable and genuinely enthusiastic about the menu. We started with the burrata appetizer – a creamy, indulgent portion served with perfectly ripe tomatoes and a drizzle of aged balsamic that had us savoring every bite.

For mains, the handmade pappardelle with wild boar ragu was exceptional. The pasta had that perfect al dente texture you can only get from fresh noodles, and the rich, slowly-simmered sauce spoke of hours of careful preparation. My dining companion's osso buco was equally impressive – the meat fell off the bone, and the risotto beneath was creamy perfection.

## Service
The service struck that sweet spot of being attentive without being intrusive. Our water glasses never went empty, and Maria checked in at just the right moments. When we mentioned celebrating an anniversary, they surprised us with a complimentary tiramisu that was the perfect end to our meal.

## Value
While not bargain dining, the prices are fair for the quality and portion sizes. Entrees range from $18-28, and given the fresh ingredients and evident care in preparation, it feels like good value.

## Minor Notes
The only small critique would be that the acoustics can make it slightly noisy when full, and reservations are definitely recommended as this place fills up quickly – a testament to its quality.

**Would I return?** Absolutely. Rare Kitchen has earned a spot on our regular rotation, and I'm already planning to bring friends who appreciate authentic Italian cuisine served with genuine hospitality.
